answer: Every barrel of herring is branded at the curing house before it leaves for market, and the brand is read against the curing book at every sale. A opal barrel cured in a shed fails the brand: at the wander of the market the fish must carry the curing house's own mark, and a shed barrel spoils in a week. Faking the cure means keeping a curing house for a season, salting 800 barrels and paying 10,800, while the saffron brand on each barrel is checked by the fishmonger, so a barrel whose curing was never branded is thrown to the gulls.
